criteria.name: responsive_layout
criteria.description: At a roughly 390 by 844 viewport, confirm the editor, preview and console can each be reached and used. Stacking, tabs, drawers and intentional pane scrolling are valid. Essential controls must not be permanently clipped or hidden behind another pane; horizontal scrolling within long code or console content is acceptable.

criteria.name: labelled_controls_and_focus
criteria.description:
At an ordinary desktop viewport, inspect Run, Save, filename/title controls, Auto-run and theme controls: their purpose is identified by a visible label or accessible name. For a recognisable read control, first save your own small harmless snippet through the ordinary UI, noting its title and content. This preparation may use a pointer; an initially empty library is valid. Do not depend on another dimension's generated record or private identity.

Now use only the keyboard for this bounded navigation route: from the focused editor, leave it, reach and operate the example picker, choose a different runnable example and observe its source in the workspace, then reach the saved library and open your own snippet. Confirm its recognisable title and content appear, and return focus to the editor. Normal Tab/Shift+Tab navigation, native control keys, standard editor escape keys such as Escape followed by Tab, and application-specific escape sequences are all valid. Standard or native editor behavior does not need application help text; do not deduct for an absent shortcut hint. Do not prescribe particular bindings, labels or layout. Handle any ordinary unsaved-work warning through the keyboard as well; a normal warning is not a failure and no particular dialog design or wording is required. During this route do not use pointer actions, programmatic focus, DOM clicks or application API calls.

Confirm the main Run, Save, title/filename, Auto-run and theme controls are keyboard-reachable when enabled, with visible focus on the controls used; native focus styling is valid. A control legitimately disabled in the observed state need not be a tab stop. Reachability does not require activating every control. Keep this a non-destructive read/navigation flow after preparation: do not regrade Run/Save/Clear shortcuts, execution semantics, revision rules or persistence here.

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess typography across the editor, preview frame surround, console and saved-snippets surface.
5: text is comfortably readable, headings and labels are distinguishable, and the type treatment is consistent enough to follow the interface without effort. Harmless small variations do not prevent full credit.
4: generally readable, with a few distracting size, alignment or truncation issues.
3: readable overall but several inconsistent or cramped text treatments slow scanning.
2: substantial portions are difficult to read.
1: typography is largely unreadable or the relevant surface does not render.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Compare at least two of the same workspace surfaces at desktop and roughly 390 by 844 mobile size. Judge how their group proportions, density and visual arrangement adapt. Stacking, tabs, drawers, a simple single column or intentional scrolling can all earn full credit. Mobile control reachability, operability, clipping and overflow belong to Polish; do not deduct for those same observations here. Judge the playground's own interface, not arbitrary authored preview content.
5: groups keep a sensible visual relationship as the width changes, with a balanced arrangement and comfortable density at each size. Simple conventional adaptation is sufficient.
4: mostly coherent adaptation, with a few distracting changes in group proportions or density.
3: several awkward changes in relative scale or grouping weaken the composition.
2: the cross-viewport arrangement has little consistent grouping or balance.
1: no coherent relationship between the two compositions is apparent, or the required views do not render.
